text:
Alex Newhook has 7 goals in 26 games, and every one of them is earned on chance quality: 6.75 expected goals, almost an exact match. What stands out is how few shots it has taken. He is scoring on 22.6% of his 31 shots, far above the 13.5% league rate, and our range for him tops out near 18.6%. More shots would make the goals more durable.

The bigger issue is the 5v5 share. Montreal gets 41.8% of the expected goals with him on the ice, nearly 12 points worse than without him, and Evolving-Hockey had his team's offence in the bottom 9% of forwards with him on last season. He plays 16.5 minutes a night, so this matters.

There's a new wrinkle. Dylan Larkin, now a Canadien, was set to play with Newhook and Texier against Carolina on Nov. 24 according to The Hockey News' Karine Hains, and Larkin's forecheck set up Newhook's tying goal that night for Larkin's first point in Montreal. If that line sticks, Newhook's role could look very different by December.
headline: Newhook is finishing; the 5v5 picture is the worry
